summary: Radar for 2026-10-06, GLP-1 focus. The EASD news cycle (retatrutide, EloraTZP, CagriSema, survodutide, orforglipron) has peaked, and we've covered most of it. The best openings now are safety and "life on GLP-1" questions that are just reaching mainstream news. Top 3 in order: (1) the 2.1-million-pregnancy meta-analysis in Med, which found no clearly detectable increase in risk after GLP-1 exposure around conception. It's emerging, has same-day UK pharmacy-press pickup, a big search audience and almost no creator explainers. Pair it with the JAMA finding of a 24-fold rise in postpartum prescriptions. (2) Semaglutide and NAION ("eye stroke"). A KXAN local story from 10-05 is reviving the BJO FAERS signal (Wegovy about 5× Ozempic in disproportionality). This needs a calm "how rare is it really" explainer, and we can contrast it with the observational data linking tirzepatide to lower retinopathy risk. (3) Mainstream news has picked up the petrelintide/amylin "fewer side effects" story (US News/HealthDay, 10-05), which makes our earlier emerging item a rising decoder. Practical evergreen topics with fresh hooks: nutrient gaps (vitamin D, iron) from the Lancet women's review and the paediatric 1-in-6 deficiency study; the roughly 30% lean-mass figure, with protein and strength training; rechecking thyroid TSH on levothyroxine (Epic, 21,538 patients); dopamine and "food noise" science (Wake Forest, 10-05; mostly animal data); and a Halloween/holiday eating hook. Lower priority: safiglipron, ATTAIN-Hypertension (trial design only), and a survodutide follow-up. We already covered survodutide on 10-05, so we should only revisit it with a new angle. The kidney mechanism RCT in Nature Medicine looks like REMODEL, which we covered on 10-05, so I left it out. Several items are observational or pharmacovigilance data and are marked caution. Scripts must state the study design clearly and never imply that anyone should stop, switch or change a dose.

candidates.topic: GLP-1 exposure around conception: no clearly detectable increase in miscarriage, birth defects or other pregnancy risks across 2,118,215 pregnancies (8,325 exposed), the largest meta-analysis to date (Med, City St George's, Oct 2026)
candidates.angle: 'Got pregnant on Ozempic or Mounjaro?' Calm decoder: what 'no detectable increase' means and what it doesn't. In the authors' own words, it is 'not the same as safe in pregnancy'. Cover the data gaps (exact week of exposure, later trimesters, breastfeeding) and why prescriber labels still advise stopping before a planned pregnancy. The only action point is to talk to your prescriber before trying to conceive or as soon as you know you're pregnant. Optional context: the JAMA 24-fold rise in postpartum prescriptions.
candidates.why_now: Press release and Med paper this week, with same-day pickup by Medical Xpress, The Pharmaceutical Journal and Medical Daily. 'Ozempic babies' is a long-running viral search theme. A related French Diabetologia nationwide study came out on 09-29, and the JAMA postpartum-prescription story is still in a previous snapshot. YouTube explainers of this paper are still scarce.

evidence.signal: 2.1M pregnancies, 10 studies, 8,325 exposed; no clearly detectable increase in adverse outcomes; authors stress this is not proof of safety
Mainstream pharmacy-press pickup, 10-05
Consumer framing: 'early reassurance, but stopping before pregnancy is still advised'
French nationwide study on GLP-1 RA safety in T2D pregnancy (09-29)

candidates.topic: Semaglutide and 'eye stroke' (NAION): the Austin Wegovy vision-loss story vs the actual numbers. In a BJO analysis of FAERS reports, Wegovy showed about 5× the NAION reporting signal of Ozempic; regulators call it very rare
candidates.angle: 'Can Wegovy cause sudden vision loss?' Explain what NAION is, how rare it is, and why a FAERS disproportionality signal isn't an incidence rate. State the regulator position (EMA/MHRA list it as very rare). Red flag: sudden painless vision loss in one eye means urgent eye care the same day. No stop or switch advice; tell viewers to report any vision change to their prescriber.
candidates.why_now: KXAN ran the local Austin case on 10-05 and Medical Economics' Morning Update repeated 'Wegovy may pose higher risk of eye stroke'. Law-firm pages are amplifying it. Fear content will spread fast, and there is room for a measured explainer.

evidence.signal: Local story of an Austin father's vision loss, 10-05

evidence.source: BMJ Group press release (Br J Ophthalmol)
evidence.signal: FAERS analysis: Wegovy about 5× the Ozempic signal, about 3× higher in men (reporting data, not incidence)
UK regulator update on semaglutide and NAION

candidates.topic: Petrelintide (amylin analogue): up to 10.7% average weight loss at 42 weeks vs 1.7% on placebo, with GI side effects described as closer to placebo (ZUPREME-1, Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology). Now in US News: 'fewer side effects than GLP-1s'
candidates.angle: Headline decoder: 'Does petrelintide really mean less nausea than semaglutide?' How amylin differs from GLP-1. Give the trial numbers next to placebo, and make clear there was no head-to-head with semaglutide or tirzepatide. Note that it's still in phase 2 and not approved as of Oct 2026, and why combinations (CagriSema, EloraTZP) are where amylin may matter most.
keywords: new weight loss drug fewer side effects
candidates.why_now: This was emerging in our 09-30 snapshot. HealthDay/US News syndicated it to mainstream readers on 10-05, Rutgers and Penn are pushing explainers, and Drug Discovery News and TIKR are covering the 'amylin era'. Creator coverage is still thin.

evidence.signal: Mainstream: 'New class of weight-loss drugs may have fewer side effects than GLP-1s', 10-05
ZUPREME-1 phase 2 RCT published
'The next generation of weight-loss drugs is almost here', 10-01

candidates.topic: Does tirzepatide protect your eyes? Linked to lower diabetic retinopathy risk vs lifestyle care alone in about 174,000 matched adults with diabetes and overweight/obesity (Ophthalmology, observational), plus a new Medical Economics mention (10-03)
candidates.angle: A named-drug benefit beyond weight with a named comparator: 'Tirzepatide and diabetic eye disease: 0.49% vs 1.2% (new mild retinopathy at 1 year)'. Say clearly that it's observational ('linked to'). Contrast it with the earlier semaglutide retinopathy questions from SUSTAIN-6, framed as separate studies. Close with: keep your annual diabetic eye exam.
candidates.why_now: Medical Economics flagged 'tirzepatide tied to lower diabetic eye disease risk' on 10-03. It pairs naturally with this week's semaglutide eye-stroke news cycle, so eye health is a hot search cluster right now.

evidence.signal: Tirzepatide linked to lower eye-disease risk in about 174,000 matched patients
Incident mild NPDR 0.49% vs 1.2%; fewer injections and laser treatments
'No increased retinopathy risk seen with tirzepatide'

candidates.topic: Nutrient gaps on semaglutide and tirzepatide: the Lancet women's health review flags low vitamin D, iron, magnesium, potassium and choline intake, and estimates about 30% of weight lost is lean mass
candidates.angle: 'Eating less on Mounjaro or Wegovy? The 5 nutrients that drop first.' Practical and positive: protein first, plus food sources of vitamin D, iron and magnesium. Ask your clinician whether blood tests make sense. Include the kidney/protein caveat and no supplement dosing. Say that the 30% lean-mass figure is an average from body-composition data, and that strength training and protein are the evidence-based mitigations.
candidates.why_now: Nutritional Outlook covered the Lancet Obstetrics, Gynaecology & Women's Health review on 10-05. Food & Wine ran 'Taking a GLP-1? Here's how to get the nutrition you need' on 10-05, GIANT grocery launched GLP-1 nutrition services, and Retail Dive covered how GLP-1 users are reshaping retail. Consumer demand for 'what to eat' content is high.

evidence.signal: Lancet review: about 30% lean mass loss; inadequate vitamin D, potassium, choline, magnesium and iron intake
Women are the predominant GLP-1 users, and research gaps remain

candidates.topic: Children on GLP-1s: 1 in 6 (16.8%) aged 10–17 were diagnosed with a nutritional deficiency within a year, mostly vitamin D (12.4%). Only 5% got nutrition counselling within 30 days (Childhood Obesity, 2,031 youths, claims data)
candidates.angle: For parents: 'Is your teen on semaglutide? What this study found and what to ask the care team.' Positive framing: GLP-1s are approved for adolescents with obesity, and nutrition support is the missing piece. Make clear the data is observational claims data with no comparison group. No dosing; point parents to the paediatric care team.
candidates.why_now: The Northwestern release (late Sept) has been syndicated across Scripps local TV this week (NBC26, LEX18, WCPO), Yahoo Health and Men's Journal. 'Sharp increase in GLP-1 use among children ages 8 to 11' (News4JAX) and 'What parents should know' segments are running on 10-05.

evidence.signal: 16.8% with a nutritional deficiency in year 1; vitamin D 12.4%; counselling gap
Local TV syndication

candidates.topic: On levothyroxine and a GLP-1? Weight loss of more than 5 lb was linked to measurable TSH drops in 21,538 people with hypothyroidism (Epic Research), so clinicians may recheck thyroid levels
candidates.angle: 'Semaglutide and your thyroid medicine: why your doctor might order a TSH test.' Explain the mechanism: less body weight and changes in absorption, not a direct drug interaction. Say that no dedicated trials exist in Hashimoto's. The action is a conversation with your clinician, never changing your own dose. Briefly cover the thyroid-cancer boxed-warning question and the evidence status in humans.
candidates.why_now: A Stacker feature syndicated widely on 10-05 (KEYT, Tucson.com, Griffin Daily News, Bryan Times). Hypothyroidism is common in our 25–65 audience, and almost no GLP-1 creators cover it.

evidence.signal: Epic Research: 21,538 hypothyroid GLP-1 users; >5 lb loss linked to TSH drop; recheck TSH after weight loss
Lean body mass predicts levothyroxine requirement

candidates.topic: Does semaglutide quiet 'food noise' in the brain? GLP-1 receptors in the nucleus accumbens and the amygdala-dopamine circuit lower the reward value of high-calorie food (Wake Forest explainer, 10-05; mostly animal studies)
candidates.angle: Our best formula, a search-style mechanism question about a named drug: 'Does Ozempic change your brain's cravings?' Explain the circuit simply and say honestly which parts are mouse studies vs human imaging. Mention that 'food noise' is a patient term, not a measured endpoint. Include the bonus mouse finding (less motivated wheel running) with a clear 'mice only' label.
candidates.why_now: Wake Forest published its feature on 10-05 and Neuroscience News is covering the circuit work. 'Food noise' is a steady high-volume search, and the playbook's #1 GLP-1 Short was this type of honest mechanism question.

evidence.signal: 'What the neuroscience of motivation has to say about GLP-1 drugs', 10-05
Amygdala–dopamine circuit reduces motivation to seek food
Semaglutide reduces motivated running in mice (preprint, animal)

candidates.topic: Muscle vs fat on tirzepatide and semaglutide: about 30% of weight lost is lean mass on average (Lancet women's review). Real-world tirzepatide body-composition and structured-exercise pilot data, plus an orthopaedic surgeon's warnings
candidates.angle: 'Losing muscle on Mounjaro? What actually protects it.' Give the lean-mass share with its context (some lean-mass loss is expected with any weight loss). Cover protein targets in general terms with the kidney caveat, plus strength training 2–3×/week. Mention the new pilot data with structured exercise, labelled as a retrospective pilot. No body imagery.
candidates.why_now: Several fresh hooks landed the same week: the Lancet review (10-05), a Yahoo orthopaedic-surgeon piece (10-05), an Obesity Pillars structured-exercise pilot, J Diabetes Complications real-world tirzepatide body composition, and an Aesthet Surg J lean-mass review. This is a double-down topic in our playbook.

evidence.signal: Fat and lean mass changes with structured exercise and nutrition (retrospective pilot)
Real-world 6-month tirzepatide body composition
Lancet review: about 30% lean-mass share

candidates.topic: Halloween and holiday eating on a GLP-1: why sugary and fatty treats can feel worse on semaglutide or tirzepatide (slower gastric emptying), plus gentle swaps (People.com treat list, 10-05)
candidates.angle: 'Halloween on Mounjaro: why one fun-size bar can hit differently.' Life on GLP-1, practical and kind: smaller portions, eat slowly, stop at full, and pair treats with protein. Nausea triggers come from the GI expert review (Nutr Clin Pract, Oct 2026). No restriction or guilt messaging. Sets up a Thanksgiving follow-up.
candidates.why_now: Seasonal cycle starting: People.com ran '8 Halloween treats you'll still love while taking a GLP-1' on 10-05. Searches climb through late October, then the holiday season follows.

evidence.signal: Expert review of GI adverse effects across approved and pipeline agents (Oct 2026)
Consumer GLP-1 nutrition guidance, 10-05

candidates.topic: 'Ozempic nails': nail detachment reported by 39.3% of GLP-1 users vs 8.7% of controls in a self-reported EADV survey (575 users vs 1,329 controls). Now on Newser
candidates.angle: 'Are Ozempic nails real?' An honest myth-check: a self-reported online survey, not a trial, with recall and selection bias. Possible explanations (rapid weight loss, nutrition) are unproven. Give nail-care basics and when to see a dermatologist. Fits our 'not proven yet' honesty style.
candidates.why_now: Seen in 2 snapshots with rising momentum (66→70). Newser syndicated it on 10-05. It has a viral 'Ozempic ___' naming pattern, similar to 'Ozempic face' and 'Ozempic hair'.

evidence.signal: 'GLP-1 users report more nail detachments', 10-05

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Zepbound) plus ixekizumab (Taltz) for psoriasis with obesity, plus a nationwide JEADV cohort on GLP-1s in hidradenitis suppurativa: GLP-1s and inflammatory skin disease
candidates.angle: Benefits beyond weight with named drugs: 'Can tirzepatide help psoriasis?' Explain the inflammation link and what Lilly reported at Fall Clinical 2026, attributed as company data. Contrast it with observational HS data. Make clear it's not an approved psoriasis treatment as of Oct 2026.
candidates.why_now: Lilly announced 21 presentations at Fall Clinical 2026, including Taltz + Zepbound. Clin Dermatol published a psoriasis review (10-01) and JEADV an HS cohort (10-03). Few creators connect GLP-1s with skin disease.

evidence.signal: GLP-1 RAs in hidradenitis suppurativa: nationwide cohort, 10-03
GLP-1 RAs in psoriasis management, review, 10-01
Taltz + Zepbound combo data for psoriasis and obesity

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide over 3 years in adults with obesity/overweight and prediabetes: what weight nadirs and regain looked like (SURMOUNT-1 analysis, Obesity Pillars)
candidates.angle: 'What happens to your weight in year 2 and 3 on Mounjaro?' Explain that plateaus are normal and what 'regain' meant in the trial while people were still on treatment. Name the population (SURMOUNT-1 prediabetes subgroup, without diabetes). Habits that help keep results going.
candidates.why_now: New SURMOUNT-1 3-year analysis is indexed (09-18). Plateau questions are among the most-asked by people on long-term treatment.

evidence.signal: Weight nadirs and regain during 3 years of tirzepatide in obesity/overweight + prediabetes

candidates.topic: Switching from GLP-1 shots to the Wegovy pill (oral semaglutide 25 mg): 4.1% further average weight loss at 3 months in 194 people (OCTANE, Ro telehealth real-world data)
candidates.angle: 'Does the Wegovy pill work as well as the shot?' Put the pill's own OASIS trial data first. Present OCTANE as a small, short, single-platform, non-randomised study with no comparison group. Any switch is a prescriber decision. Never promote the platform.
candidates.why_now: Seen in 2 snapshots. Patient Care Online covered it again on 10-05, and Reuters/CNBC covered it on 09-30. Search queries like 'is wegovy pills effective' and 'is the wegovy pill safe' appear in today's feeds.

evidence.signal: People switching to the Wegovy pill kept losing weight (real-world)
194 participants on the pill for 3 months

candidates.topic: Safiglipron, another oral GLP-1 pill: non-inferior to dapagliflozin for A1C at all doses and superior at 90 mg (−0.40% difference) in adults with T2D in China (OUTSTAND-2, Nature Medicine); weight loss similar (−4.17% vs −3.60%)
candidates.angle: 'The pill race: did safiglipron beat an SGLT2 pill?' A decoder with the named comparator. The A1C win is real but modest, the weight result was a tie, and the trial ran only in China. Where it sits next to orforglipron (Foundayo) and the Wegovy pill, framed as separate trials.
candidates.why_now: Two Nature Medicine papers (placebo-controlled and vs dapagliflozin) appeared within a week, and Nature reported it on 10-05. Interest in pills is high ('semaglutide pills' and 'foundayo vs ozempic' are both active queries), but search volume for the drug name itself is small.

evidence.signal: OUTSTAND-2 phase 3 vs dapagliflozin, 98 sites in China
Placebo-controlled trial in early T2D

candidates.topic: Survodutide follow-up: how a GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist differs from tirzepatide's GLP-1/GIP. SYNCHRONIZE-2: up to 13.1% at 76 weeks vs 3.1% placebo in adults with overweight/obesity + T2D (NEJM; efficacy estimand)
candidates.angle: Only if we want a mechanism follow-up to the 10-05 piece: 'Why does survodutide target glucagon? The liver-fat angle.' Use the paper's figures (752, not the press release's 755), and frame any comparison with tirzepatide as cross-trial.
candidates.why_now: NEJM and EASD coverage is still running (AJMC, Healio), but we already published on 10-05, so this is only worth doing with a different mechanism or liver angle.

evidence.signal: Survodutide once weekly in adults with obesity and T2D
Up to 13.1% vs 3.1%; A1C down up to 1.21 points from 7.4%
